test_title: PYST 34 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 25 Nov, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Convert this sentence to active voice:

"Uninterrupted personal time is often disturbed by mobile notifications."

options.text: Mobile notifications are often disturbing uninterrupted personal time.
Mobile notifications disturb uninterrupted personal time.
Uninterrupted personal time disturbs mobile notifications.
Uninterrupted personal time has been disturbed by mobile notifications

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Active voice structure:** The "doer" of the action (the agent) becomes the subject of the sentence.
 
• In the original passive sentence: "Uninterrupted personal time is often disturbed by mobile notifications," the agent is **"mobile notifications."**
 
• To convert to active voice: Place the agent "mobile notifications" at the beginning as the subject.
 
• Change the passive verb form "is... disturbed" (present simple passive) to the active form **"disturb"** (present simple active).
 
• Place the original subject "uninterrupted personal time" in the object position after the verb.
 
• Maintain the adverb "often" before the main verb to keep the original frequency of the action.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Mobile notifications disturb uninterrupted personal time."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Mobile notifications are often disturbing uninterrupted personal time." – This uses the present continuous tense, which changes the original simple present meaning.
 
• **Option 3:** "Uninterrupted personal time disturbs mobile notifications." – This reverses the logic of the sentence, making the time the "doer."
 
• **Option 4:** "Uninterrupted personal time has been disturbed by mobile notifications" – This is still in the passive voice and changes the tense to present perfect.
